what_the_writer_read:
Threat:
- ThreatFox, about the indicator only: 198.51.100.77:8443 (ip:port) is listed as win.nanocore, threat type botnet command and control.
- Background not evidence: NanoCore RAT: Windows remote-access trojan. The victim connects out to an operator-chosen host and port and speaks NanoCore's own protocol: length-prefixed, DES-encrypted frames over plain TCP. That channel carries no TLS handshake and never uses UDP.
- the flagged address 198.51.100.77 is in AS64510 Example VPS B.V. (NL).
Host:
- the address appears on 35 day(s) of campus history from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-24, with traffic to or from a known remote address on 35.
- none of the products with a known purpose appears on its days of campus history.
- on 2026-11-22 it used 10 distinct services (the campus median was 13 and the 90th percentile 22) and moved 9.2 MB.
- names it used on the most of the 4 day(s) read, with the number of days: juniper-cloud.test (4), notify-hub.test (4), chalk-video.test (3), comet-games.test (3), drift-books.test (3), ember-code.test (3), ember-docs.test (3), hazel-health.test (3).
What happened:
- The host's contact with the flagged address: 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name, 132 minute(s) on 2026-11-22..2026-11-24, first 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC, last 2026-11-24 23:30 UTC; 34.3 KB received, 55.2 KB sent.
- 198.51.100.77 carried at most 0 registered domain(s): not shown to be shared.
- From 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-24 (4 day(s)): after the first match the next destination new to this host was harbor-anchor-code.test, 13.6 h later; 3 new named destination(s) (this address used 10 distinct services on 2026-11-22, against a campus median of 13) and 1 network(s) with no name in all; uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations: none.
Outcome:
- Outcome: review. We kept this case for review because: a scheduled low-volume contact.
- 3 items; the first: scheduled low-volume contact with 198.51.100.77 on 2026-11-22: 36 minutes, mean gap 30.0 min, over 17.5 h.
- No ordinary reason found: 3 contact(s) with 198.51.100.77 (no TLS name, so no site can be named). In detail: no TLS name: the contact cannot be attributed to a site.
Next steps:
- Identify the device: the address lease (DHCP, network access control or VPN logs) for HOST from 2026-11-22 05:45 UTC to 2026-11-23 00:30 UTC, and on the later match day(s) 2026-11-23..2026-11-24. An address is not a device.
- Find which process makes the scheduled contact; a schedule this regular is a program, not a person.
- Identify the process behind contact 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name at 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC.
- Check the host's endpoint record for a NanoCore client process and its persistence (a .NET executable started from the user profile) and for outbound TCP from it.

paragraphs.summary: ThreatFox lists the address 198.51.100.77 on port 8443 as a win.nanocore botnet command-and-control indicator. We found the campus device at 10.30.1.33 reached it from 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC to 24 Nov 2026 23:30 UTC, and we kept this case for review because the contact runs on a regular schedule with no TLS name to attribute it to a site. The next step is to identify the device from its address lease for those dates and check its endpoint record for a NanoCore client.
paragraphs.threat: ThreatFox lists 198.51.100.77:8443 as win.nanocore with the threat type botnet command and control. NanoCore is a Windows remote-access trojan whose client connects out to an operator-chosen host and port and uses its own encrypted protocol over plain TCP, without a TLS handshake.
paragraphs.host: Between 21 Oct 2026 and 24 Nov 2026 the device at 10.30.1.33 appeared on 35 days of campus history, with traffic to or from a known remote address on each. On 22 Nov 2026 it used 10 distinct services and moved 9.2 MB. Across the days we read, the names it reached most often were juniper-cloud.test and notify-hub.test, each on 4 days. No product with a known purpose appears on its days of history.
paragraphs.contact: The device at 10.30.1.33 contacted 198.51.100.77 on 8443/TCP with no TLS name for 132 minutes across 22 Nov 2026 to 24 Nov 2026, first at 06:00 UTC on 22 Nov and last at 23:30 UTC on 24 Nov. It received 34.3 KB and sent 55.2 KB. We found no evidence that the address is shared with other domains.
paragraphs.why: The case stays open because the contact recurs on a fixed schedule: on 22 Nov 2026 it lasted 36 minutes with a mean gap of 30.0 minutes over 17.5 hours. We found no ordinary reason for the three contacts, and because they carry no TLS name we cannot tie them to any site.
paragraphs.after: From 21 Nov 2026 to 24 Nov 2026 the device at 10.30.1.33 reached 3 new named destinations, the first being harbor-anchor-code.test 13.6 hours after the first match, and one network with no name. On 22 Nov 2026 it used 10 services against a campus median of 13. We found no uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations.
paragraphs.conclusion: We can say the device at 10.30.1.33 had a scheduled, low-volume contact with an address ThreatFox lists for NanoCore on 8443/TCP, and how much data moved each way; we cannot say which program made the contact or what the device is doing. The next steps are to identify the device from its DHCP, network access control or VPN lease for 22 Nov 2026 05:45 UTC to 24 Nov 2026; find which process makes the scheduled contact; and check the endpoint record for a NanoCore client and its persistence and outbound TCP.
